motivation: In 2007 Lorimer, Bailes, McLaughlin and colleagues reported a single, millisecond-long, highly dispersed radio burst in archival Parkes data whose dispersion measure placed it far beyond our Galaxy. That discovery opened an entirely new class of astrophysical transients. Fast radio bursts are now detected by the thousand, localised to host galaxies, and linked to magnetars. They have become a new tool for fundamental physics. Their dispersion measures have located the 'missing' cosmic baryons, measured the intergalactic medium, and constrain the Hubble constant, the photon mass, the equivalence principle and the distance-duality relation. Bailes' leadership of pulsar and transient programmes, including on MeerKAT, and McLaughlin's discovery of rotating radio transients helped turn a single anomalous pulse into a field. Few discoveries this century have so changed how we probe the Universe.
